title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect + reconnect/resume + server timeout hardening
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: streaming sessions were vulnerable to orphaned server work and token leakage when clients canceled mid-stream, disconnected abruptly, or reconnected to resume. This PR implements a set of lifecycle controls: (1) explicit client-initiated cancel semantics with guaranteed server-side cancellation of active generation tasks, (2) improved disconnect detection and a short grace window for reconnect/resume using a resumable session token, (3) server-side idle and request timeouts with observability hooks and configurable backoff to avoid wasted GPU cycles, and (4) compatibility glue for the OpenAI-compat streaming layer so function/tool-calling and structured output flows can safely resume and deduplicate partial events. Changes are designed to be backward-compatible: old clients keep current behavior, new clients can opt into resumable sessions via a streamingSessionResume header. Checklist: - [x] runtime: cancel RPC and task abort handlers - [x] API: streamingSessionResume header and server validation - [x] SDKs: JS/TS and Python resume helpers and example - [x] telemetry: new metrics (stream.session.resume, stream.session.cancel, stream.session.orphaned) - [x] e2e: integration tests for cancel, disconnect+reconnect, and timeout cases - [x] docs: redwood-docs entry and OpenAI-compat note - [x] perf: microbench against continuous batching to ensure no regressions. Test plan: unit tests for abort path, integration harness runs against perf-canary, manual verification using redwood-quickstarts streaming example, and a canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 24h. Backwards compatibility notes: resumable flows are opt-in; servers will accept new header but will not change behavior for legacy clients. Related: ENG-3421 (streaming stability), ENG-3530 (streaming resume UX), SUP-781 (customer incident affecting reconnects).
